question.text: In a Young’s double slit experiment, the intensities at two points, for the path difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math> being the wavelength of light used) are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> respectively. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> denotes the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi></math>.

solution.text:
As we know, resultant intensity is given by,

I=4I0 cos2Δϕ2 and phase difference can be written as ∆ϕ=2πλ∆x.

For first case:

I1=4I0 cos22πλ×λ4=4I0 cos2π4=2I0

For second case:

I2=4I0 cos22πλ×λ3=4I0 cos22π3=I0

Therefore, required value ofI1+I2I0=3.
